+# Source boundary and complete cost
+
+All gate indices and original register identifiers below are zero-based.
+The object is the exact PR589 word pinned in `SOURCES.json`.
+
+## 1. The legal late read
+
+Let `x` be source77, `q` helper470, and `r` receiver444. In A, the only two
+uses of q are:
+
+```text
+A[230]  at frame79: q += x
+A[1993] at frame79: r += q
+```
+
+There is no B use of q. The copied totals do not include q. Before the second
+operation, exact replay on all independent initial columns gives
+`x = x_in` and `q = q_in + x_in` over F2. In particular, a borrowed helper is
+not treated as initially zero.
+
+Source77 begins at frame79, the line `[77]`. A[426] reads it at frame186,
+whose lines are `[33,77]` and whose rational dimension is two. Receiver444
+is still at frame0 before A[1993]. Its next gate is A[1994] at frame509,
+which contains frame186 and has dimension four. The next source77 read is
+B[35] at frame186. Thus the new gate
+
+```text
+at frame186: r += x
+```
+
+has valid entry frames, common-frame operands, and valid next frames for both
+operands. The original frame79 read of x at this time would be a descent
+from frame186 and is invalid. The new gate does not move x early.
+
+Delete A[230], replace A[1993] as above, and remove q from the physical stock.
+Subtract one from every old identifier greater than 470. Keep the E8 geometry,
+all other A gates, B, scatter and all copied totals, subject to that renaming.
+
+The rational frame check and the native legality checker give these paths:
+
+| Old register | Old path | New path |
+|---|---|---|
+| 77 | `[79,186,509,386,560,1]` | same |
+| 444 | `[0,79,509,392,513,1]` | `[0,186,509,392,513,1]` |
+| 470 | `[0,79,1]` | removed |
+
+Every other surviving register path is equal under the renaming. The complete
+lists are in `FRAME-PATHS.json`. All 636 original frames remain in the catalogue.
+
+## 2. Dirty state and literal restoration
+
+The removed read used to add both `x_in` and `q_in` to r. The new read adds
+`x_in`. Thus deletion changes a dirty-helper column; it is not a free scalar
+substitution inside the old compensated word.
+
+Rebuild D from the exact map of A, scatter and B. D contains only frame-zero
+helper-to-target operations. In this case the rebuilt D is exactly the old D
+with its 55 q operands deleted and all other identifiers renamed. It changes
+from 18,085 to 18,030 scalar ADDs. Every remaining helper contribution is paid.
+
+Rebuild C as the literal reversed list of all A/B operations that write a
+source or helper, at the full frame. Reuse of the old C would not restore the
+changed basis. C has 2,573 gates instead of 2,574. The original interleaved
+checker verifies H1-H5 and the conclusions `U_block_form`, `J_identity`,
+`C_is_U_inverse`, and `K_equals_D` on the changed word.
+
+The complete order is D, A, nine COPY/scatter/ERASE episodes, B, C, then all
+required final MOVEs. Exact F2 replay returns every source and helper to its
+initial value and maps each target `y_i` to `y_i + x_i` for every dirty column.
+The source checker also verifies the punctured-line geometry and rank-seven
+copied totals. No decoder change is used.
+
+Removing A[230] and its C inverse saves two ADDs. The compensation change saves
+55 more. The total is 57. The independent literal emitter and the unchanged
+native exporter produce the same record list for each complete word.
+
+The signed native inverse uses negated ADDs and the original unchanged center
+for reverse COPY/ERASE blocks. The existing native checkers and parent checker
+replay this inverse. The cancellation-free forward and reverse bounds remain
+49,347 and 1,113,070. Their charged precision bounds remain 93 local bits and
+177 nine-stage bits, within the inherited 104/192 allowances.
+
+## 3. Local recursive charges
+
+Deletion of q removes rank-one and rank-seven MOVEs. Moving r first to the
+rank-two frame changes its first two increments from `(1,3)` to `(2,2)`.
+No other path changes. Therefore the exact profile difference is
+
+```text
+rank 1: -2; rank 2: +2; rank 3: -1; rank 7: -1.
+```
+
+The complete profiles are:
+
+| Child rank | R439 | R438 |
+|---|---:|---:|
+| 1 | 1323 | 1321 |
+| 2 | 1342 | 1344 |
+| 3 | 79 | 78 |
+| 4 | 44 | 44 |

+The paid rank mass falls from 5,129 to 5,121. It still satisfies

+## 4. Hosting and returned idle rank

+Use the same nine-stage parent, four DATA pairs and 32 replicas. Expand the

+These checks use the complete profile above and the inherited surcharge. They

+# R438 bit supplier from a legal source boundary
+
+This finite construction removes one helper from the selected PR589 R439 bit
+word. At one late read, source77 is still unchanged and is available at
+frame186. Receiver444 can enter that frame before its next operation.
+The word reads source77 directly, removes helper470, and rebuilds the literal
+cleanup and dirty-target compensation.
+
+The complete nine-stage hosted invoice improves bit `c` from
+`0.001733427039589844234749` to **`0.001734176288479865766692`**.
+This package does not claim a new kappa. The selected PR942 complex value
+`0.001664727258740678855772` is smaller than both bit values. The selected
+conditional kappa remains `0.001661960547713947` at the research base.
+
+| Complete charge | PR589 R439 | This R438 word |
+|---|---:|---:|
+| Local helper registers | 439 | 438 |
+| Local native ADDs, including D and C | 24,305 | 24,248 |
+| Local native records | 27,234 | 27,175 |
+| Local paid rank mass | 5,129 | 5,121 |
+| Hosted residual roles, nine stages and 32 replicas | 126,432 | 126,144 |
+| Paid recursive children, including idle remainders | 904,896 | 904,320 |
+| Emitted local records across all 288 calls | 7,843,392 | 7,826,400 |
+| Hosted paid rank mass | 1,808,352 | 1,808,352 |
+| Live DATA / physical registers | 28,416 / 28,425 | 28,416 / 28,425 |
+| Prefix bits / charged bits | 177 / 192 | 177 / 192 |
+| Two-level coefficient bits / charged bits | 393 / 512 | 393 / 512 |
+
+The same upstream word is used on both sides. No local circuit saving from
+another PR is included. The source path is unchanged. The only surviving
+register whose path changes is receiver444:
+`[0,79,509,392,513,1]` becomes `[0,186,509,392,513,1]`.
+The removed helper had path `[0,79,1]`.
+
+## Reproduce
+
+Use Python 3.11 or later with NumPy, SymPy and SciPy, a C++17 compiler, and
+Boost headers. These are the inherited native pipeline requirements.
+From the repository root, run the following command. The output directory
+must not exist. Set `BOOST_INCLUDE` if the headers are outside `/usr/include`.
+
+```sh
+BOOST_INCLUDE=/opt/homebrew/include python3 -I -B research/bit-boundary-persistence/verify.py --output /tmp/r438-source-boundary
+```
+
+The last line is:
+
+```text
+PASS_R438_SOURCE_BOUNDARY R=439->438 ADDs=24305->24248 paid_calls=904896->904320 c=0.001734176288479865766692 controls=6 no_new_kappa
+```
+
+The command uses one worker. It rebuilds both words, checks all source pins,
+compiles and runs the original native checkers, emits both complete hosted
+schedules, audits them, and computes both invoices. It compares the new
+certificate with `CERTIFICATE.json`. It retains the generated words, native
+records, schedules, exact receipts, command list and logs in the output
+directory. It does not run a hosting search.
+
+`SOURCES.json` pins the two complete dependency packages and two selected
+context records at base `8bddbee377e2f3ce1f1247196c4b290d55767d20`.
+The packages include source notices and unused historical controls. The selected
+bit head is `a5afc8c6169ea61ba7c51dfd3cade02cc7b13b46` (PR589).
+Regenerated words are compared by canonical JSON, not gzip container bytes.
+`FRAME-PATHS.json` gives each physical register path in register order.
+
+The recorded run used macOS 26.6.1 arm64, Python 3.14.7, NumPy 2.5.4,
+SymPy 1.14.0 and SciPy 1.18.1. The command records the compiler command and
+Boost version-header hash in `RESULT.json`. Remote CI is not claimed.
+
+## Verification and scope
+
+The local checker covers every arbitrary dirty input column: 661 before the
+change and 660 after it. The original checker accepts H1-H5, the interleaved
+interface, all nine rank-seven copied totals, and the exact full-frame inverse.
+An independent literal record builder agrees with the original exporter.
+The native C++ checker covers 5, 9 and 11 stages on both words; all 96 omitted
+bridge controls reject. Each nine-stage parent audit rejects 17 mutations.
+Each whole-residual hosting audit rejects 16 mutations.
+
+Six new controls reject a changed source77, another carrier use, the late
+source read in frame79, omitted restoration, omitted compensation, and a
+missing returned idle charge. A neutral ADD pair passes and is charged twice.
+The [proof](PROOF.md) gives the boundary and complete invoice derivation.
+
+The caller uses a compressed exact cover schedule. It does not enumerate the
+astronomical address cover. The all-size bit/Gaussian compiler, common labels,
+mutable-source realization, whole-call correlated-helper hosting, common grid,
+tape, precision and analytic contracts remain inherited assumptions. Finite
+checks do not prove the full multiplication theorem or a practical speedup.
+
+The inherited `assemble9.py` also checks its historical PR548 outer arithmetic
+against a cited complex receipt. This is not a replay of the selected PR942
+complex construction or its full outer assembly. The selected record is only
+used for the stated comparison. The eleven-stage native scalar check is run;
+an eleven-stage hosted invoice is not claimed.
+
+## Relation to other work
+
+The initial candidate was to retain a helper basis between adjacent native
+calls. The selected caller alternates the DATA roles and advances to other
+hosted slices. A scalar cancellation does not establish a legal retained
+source and owner boundary there. This package instead changes one intra-call
+source access. It makes no repeated-call cancellation claim.
+
+[PR953](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/953) batches dyadic
+queries with a shared unchanged source and target. It does not provide this
+selected caller boundary. [PR997](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/997)
+has a signed Hadamard recursive interface. Its batch is not composed here.
+[PR980](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/980), head
+`ba1cf68bef0c97dfb120add04304e2de0db6f29c`, retains R439 and all frame paths.
+[PR1001](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1001), head
+`fbf54e6c95c47a3891eb7e8ed063b5198e920f3f`, changes B at frame506. This word
+leaves B unchanged after register renaming and changes helper stock and a
+source-access frame. Their savings are not added to this result.
+[PR1015](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1015), head
+`7588c797f4a4e9f2b9fc663cfa6e35afcac05e06`, changes all ten phase-B blocks
+and their literal cleanup. Its pinned `candidate_word` changes B and C only.
+It retains R439, A, D and the paid recursive profile. This candidate changes
+A, C, D, one path and R, while it preserves every B gate under renaming.
+No composition of the two words is tested or claimed.
+
+The full-frame obstruction in PR827 fixes A/scatter/B. The closed class in
+PR933 fixes the helper stock and cleanup structure. This construction changes
+those restrictions. Source inlining and early helper retirement are prior
+ideas; PR429/515 and PR433/437 contain related work. No general mechanism
+priority, circuit optimum, or absence of other valid boundaries is claimed.
+See [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) for contributor credit and AI disclosure.

+def bits(mask):
+    while mask:
+        bit = mask & -mask
+        yield bit.bit_length() - 1
+        mask ^= bit
+
+
+def rank(rows):
+    basis = {}
+    for values in rows:
+        row = list(map(Fraction, values))
+        for pivot, old in sorted(basis.items()):
+            value = row[pivot]
+            row = [a - value * b for a, b in zip(row, old)]
+        pivot = next((i for i, x in enumerate(row) if x), None)
+        if pivot is not None:
+            value = row[pivot]
+            basis[pivot] = [x / value for x in row]
+    return len(basis)

+def lifetime(word):
+    v = word['v']
+    require(word['R'] == 439 and v == 111, 'Wrong source word dimensions')
+    require(word['A'][BIRTH] == [79, HELPER, [SOURCE]], 'Carrier birth changed')
+    require(word['A'][READ] == [79, RECEIVER, [HELPER]], 'Carrier read changed')
+    occurrences = [(phase, i) for phase in ('A', 'B')
+                   for i, (_, dst, sources) in enumerate(word[phase])
+                   if HELPER in [dst, *sources]]
+    require(occurrences == [('A', BIRTH), ('A', READ)], 'Carrier has another live use')
+    require(HELPER not in word['ret'], 'Carrier is a retained copy source')
+    masks = [sum(1 << x for x in frame) for frame in word['frames']]
+    current = word['start'][:]
+    values = [1 << i for i in range(2 * v + word['R'])]
+    for frame, dst, sources in word['A'][:READ]:
+        for row in [dst, *sources]:
+            current[row] = frame
+        for source in sources:
+            values[dst] ^= values[source]
+    require(values[SOURCE] == 1 << SOURCE, 'Source changed before the late read')
+    require(values[HELPER] == (1 << SOURCE) ^ (1 << HELPER), 'Carrier contents changed')
+    require(current[SOURCE] == FRAME, 'Source boundary frame changed')
+    used = [SOURCE, RECEIVER]
+    before = {str(row): current[row] for row in used}
+    following = {}
+    for row in used:
+        next_frame = next(frame for frame, dst, sources in word['A'][READ + 1:] + word['B']

+        require(masks[current[row]] & ~masks[FRAME] == 0, 'Illegal source access frame')

+    return {'birth': BIRTH, 'read': READ, 'helper': HELPER, 'source': SOURCE,
+            'receiver': RECEIVER, 'new_frame': FRAME, 'before': before,
+            'next_frame': following, 'source_unchanged': True,
+            'retained_copy_uses': 0}

+def rebuild_compensation(word):
+    v = word['v']
+    count = 2 * v + word['R']
+    values = [1 << i for i in range(count)]
+    for frame, dst, sources in word['A']:
+        for source in sources:
+            values[dst] ^= values[source]

+    for frame, dst, sources in word['B']:

+            values[dst] ^= values[source]

+        if residue:
+            result.append([0, v + target, list(bits(residue))])

+    result['final'].pop(HELPER)

+    result['R'] -= 1
+    result['stats']['extra_carriers'] -= 1

+    return result

+

+    dimensions = [rank(word['lines'][i] for i in frame) for frame in word['frames']]
+    values = [1 << i for i in range(count)]

+        require(masks[previous] & ~masks[frame] == 0, 'Frame descent')
+        if previous != frame:

+            profile[delta] += 1
+            records.append([0, row, previous, frame, delta, 0])
+            current[row] = frame
+            paths[row].append(frame)
+    def gates(phase, number):

+            for row in [dst, *sources]:

+    gates('D', 1)
+    gates('A', 2)
+    for index, row in enumerate(word['ret']):
+        frame = current[row]

+    gates('C', 5)

+    bounds = []
+    for reverse in (False, True):

+        maximum = 1
+        for op, dst, src, coefficient, frame, phase in reversed(records) if reverse else records:

+            elif op == (2 if reverse else 3):

+    local = 64 * bounds[0] ** 3 * bounds[1] ** 2

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Verify the source boundary, complete native words and hosted invoice.
+
+Ali Romman, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0.
+"""
+import argparse
+import copy
+import hashlib
+import importlib.util
+import json
+from collections import Counter
+from fractions import Fraction
+from pathlib import Path
+import tempfile
+
+PACKAGE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+ROOT = PACKAGE.parent.parent
+
+
+def module(name):
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, PACKAGE / (name + '.py'))
+    value = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(value)
+    return value
+
+
+build = module('build')
+pipeline = module('pipeline')
+
+
+def digest(value):
+    return hashlib.sha256(build.canonical(value)).hexdigest()
+
+
+def boundary(word, local):
+    receipt = build.lifetime(word)
+    old, new = (local[name]['paths'] for name in ('baseline', 'candidate'))
+    changes = {}
+    for row, path in enumerate(old):
+        if row != build.HELPER and path != new[row - (row > build.HELPER)]:
+            changes[str(row)] = [path, new[row - (row > build.HELPER)]]
+    build.require(changes == {'444': [[0, 79, 509, 392, 513, 1],
+                                     [0, 186, 509, 392, 513, 1]]},
+                  'Another surviving frame path changed')
+    receipt.update(changed_surviving_paths=changes, removed_path=old[build.HELPER],
+                   source_path=old[build.SOURCE],
+                   frames={str(f): {'lines': word['frames'][f],
+                           'rank': build.rank(word['lines'][i] for i in word['frames'][f])}
+                           for f in (79, 186, 509)},
+                   all_paths_sha256=digest({'baseline': old, 'candidate': new}))
+    return receipt
+
+
+def local_controls(original, candidate):
+    controls = []
+
+    def reject(name, action, reason):
+        try:
+            action()
+        except ValueError as error:
+            build.require(str(error) == reason, 'Control failed for another reason: ' + name)
+            controls.append({'name': name, 'rejection': reason})
+        else:
+            raise ValueError('Control was accepted: ' + name)
+
+    changed = copy.deepcopy(original)
+    changed['A'][426] = [186, 77, [292]]
+    reject('source77_changed_before_read', lambda: build.lifetime(changed),
+           'Source changed before the late read')
+    changed = copy.deepcopy(original)
+    changed['A'][build.READ + 2][2].append(build.HELPER)
+    reject('another_live_carrier_use', lambda: build.lifetime(changed),
+           'Carrier has another live use')
+    changed = copy.deepcopy(candidate)
+    changed['A'][build.READ - 1][0] = 79
+    reject('late_source_read_in_old_line_frame', lambda: build.replay(changed), 'Frame descent')
+    changed = copy.deepcopy(candidate)
+    changed['C'].pop(0)
+    reject('omitted_literal_restoration', lambda: build.replay(changed), 'Wrong arbitrary-dirty endpoint')
+    changed = copy.deepcopy(candidate)
+    changed['D'][0][2].pop(0)
+    reject('omitted_dirty_target_compensation', lambda: build.replay(changed), 'Wrong arbitrary-dirty endpoint')
+    # A neutral pair is legal, but both native ADDs must be paid.
+    changed = copy.deepcopy(candidate)
+    duplicate = [0, changed['D'][0][1], [changed['D'][0][2][0]]]
+    changed['D'][0:0] = [copy.deepcopy(duplicate), duplicate]
+    positive, _ = build.replay(changed)
+    clean, _ = build.replay(candidate)
+    build.require(positive['adds'] == clean['adds'] + 2 and positive['profile'] == clean['profile'],
+                  'Neutral paid ADD pair was not accepted and charged')
+    return {'rejected': controls, 'accepted_paid_neutral_pair': {'extra_adds': 2, 'same_profile': True}}
+
+
+def check_hosted_change(result, local):
+    change = result['hosting_change']
+    actual = {}
+    for name in ('baseline', 'candidate'):
+        audit = result[name]['hosted']['audit']
+        profile = {int(rank): count for rank, count in audit['profile'].items()}
+        build.require(sum(rank * count for rank, count in profile.items())
+                      == 64 * audit['live'] - audit['deficit'], 'Wrong hosted rank mass')
+        actual[name] = Counter(profile)
+    expected = actual['baseline'].copy()
+    for sign, name in ((-1, 'baseline'), (1, 'candidate')):
+        for rank, count in local[name]['profile'].items():
+            expected[int(rank)] += sign * 288 * count
+    for sign, key in ((-1, 'old_remainders'), (1, 'new_remainders')):
+        for rank, count in change[key].items():
+            expected[int(rank)] += sign * 32 * count
+    build.require(+expected == +actual['candidate'], 'Hosted profile differs from the complete recount')
+    build.require(sum(actual['baseline'].values()) - sum(actual['candidate'].values()) == 576,
+                  'Wrong paid recursive call saving')
+    return {'paid_calls': {name: sum(profile.values()) for name, profile in actual.items()},
+            'saved_calls': 576, 'returned_idle_rank': 32 * change['returned_idle_rank_per_replica']}
+
+
+def idle_control(result, local):
+    changed = copy.deepcopy(result)
+    profile = changed['candidate']['hosted']['audit']['profile']
+    delta = Counter()
+    for sign, key in ((-1, 'old_remainders'), (1, 'new_remainders')):
+        for rank, count in result['hosting_change'][key].items():
+            delta[str(rank)] += sign * 32 * count
+    for rank, count in delta.items():
+        profile[rank] = profile.get(rank, 0) - count
+    try:
+        check_hosted_change(changed, local)
+    except ValueError as error:
+        build.require(str(error) == 'Wrong hosted rank mass', 'Idle control failed for another reason')
+        return {'name': 'deleted_helper_without_returned_idle_charge', 'rejection': str(error)}
+    raise ValueError('Omitted idle charge was accepted')
+
+
+def certificate(original, local, result, selected):
+    boundary_receipt = boundary(original, local)
+    controls = local_controls(original, build.build(original))
+    controls['rejected'].append(idle_control(result, local))
+    hosted = {}
+    for name in ('baseline', 'candidate'):
+        section = result[name]['hosted']
+        # Container hashes and running times are not mathematical outputs.
+        audit = {key: value for key, value in section['audit'].items()
+                 if key not in ('template_sha256', 'seconds')}
+        parent = section['parent']
+        parent_keys = ('all_scalar_columns_restored', 'bridge_additions', 'copy_erase_episodes',
+                       'halving_integer_inequality', 'independent_unbanked_scalar_columns',
+                       'local_checks', 'local_invocations', 'scalar_stages', 'omitted_bridge_shears_rejected')
+        invoice = {key: value for key, value in section['invoice'].items() if key != 'kappa'}
+        hosted[name] = {'audit': audit, 'invoice': invoice,
+                        'parent': {key: parent[key] for key in parent_keys},
+                        'parent_controls': section['parent_audit']['mutations_rejected']}
+    old_c = Fraction(hosted['baseline']['invoice']['bit_lower'])
+    new_c = Fraction(hosted['candidate']['invoice']['bit_lower'])
+    build.require(old_c == Fraction(selected['bit_lower']) and new_c > old_c > Fraction(selected['complex_lower']),
+                  'Selected supplier comparison changed')
+    return {'status': 'PASS_R438_SOURCE_BOUNDARY_AND_FULL_HOSTED_INVOICE',
+            'base_commit': build.BASE, 'boundary': boundary_receipt,
+            'local': {name: {key: value for key, value in item.items() if key != 'paths'}
+                      for name, item in local.items()},
+            'native': {name: {key: result[name][key] for key in ('interface', 'legality', 'columns')}
+                       for name in ('baseline', 'candidate')},
+            'hosting_change': result['hosting_change'], 'hosted': hosted,
+            'paid_recount': check_hosted_change(result, local), 'controls': controls,
+            'selected_context': {key: selected[key] for key in ('kappa', 'complex_lower', 'bit_lower', 'binding')},
+            'no_new_kappa': True}
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True, help='New directory for the full replay')
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    out = args.output.resolve()
+    build.require(not out.exists(), 'Output directory already exists')
+    manifest = pipeline.read(PACKAGE / 'SOURCES.json')
+    build.require(manifest['base_commit'] == build.BASE, 'Wrong source base')
+    for name, expected in manifest['files'].items():
+        build.require(hashlib.sha256((ROOT / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == expected,
+                      'Source hash mismatch: ' + name)
+    original = build.load(ROOT / build.WORD)
+    candidate = build.build(original)
+    receipts, records = {}, {}
+    for name, word in (('baseline', original), ('candidate', candidate)):
+        receipts[name], records[name] = build.replay(word)
+    paths = {name: receipt['paths'] for name, receipt in receipts.items()}
+    build.require(paths == pipeline.read(PACKAGE / 'FRAME-PATHS.json'), 'Stored frame paths differ')
+    expected = pipeline.read(PACKAGE / 'CERTIFICATE.json')
+    for name in ('baseline', 'candidate'):
+        build.require(receipts[name]['word_sha256'] == expected['local'][name]['word_sha256'],
+                      'Constructed word differs from the certificate')
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='bit-boundary-') as temporary:
+        word_file = Path(temporary) / 'candidate.json.gz'
+        build.save(word_file, candidate)
+        result = pipeline.run(ROOT, out, {'baseline': ROOT / build.WORD, 'candidate': word_file}, receipts, records)
+    selected = pipeline.read(ROOT / 'research/community-frontier942-audit/ASSEMBLY.json')
+    observed = certificate(original, receipts, result, selected)
+    pipeline.write(out / 'CERTIFICATE.json', observed)
+    pipeline.write(out / 'FRAME-PATHS.json', paths)
+    # Compare JSON objects so histogram keys have the same string type.
+    build.require(build.canonical(pipeline.read(out / 'CERTIFICATE.json')) == build.canonical(expected),
+                  'Full certificate differs')
+    print('PASS_R438_SOURCE_BOUNDARY R=439->438 ADDs=24305->24248 '
+          'paid_calls=904896->904320 c=0.001734176288479865766692 controls=6 no_new_kappa')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+"""Exact residual bank routes for the kernel word; chafreaky with OpenAI Codex.
+
+The stored integer rows divided by two are an orthonormal basis. Entrance
+rows span E; the remaining rows span E-perp. A coordinate permutation sends
+the latter to the assigned contiguous block in a width-64 bank. This gives
+an explicit rational isometry, with only powers of two in denominators.
+"""
+from collections import Counter, deque
+from tile_m import tile
+
+
+def placement(widths, replicas=32):
+    assert replicas > 0 and replicas % 8 == 0
+    by_width = {}
+    for rep in range(replicas):
+        for helper, width in enumerate(widths):
+            assert 0 < width <= 8
+            by_width.setdefault(width, deque()).append((rep, helper))
+    patterns = tile({w: len(q) for w, q in by_width.items()}, 64)
+    result = {}
+    bank = 0
+    for widths_in_bank, count in patterns:
+        for _ in range(count):
+            offset = 0
+            for width in widths_in_bank:
+                key = by_width[width].popleft()
+                result[key] = (bank, offset, width)
+                offset += width
+            assert offset == 64
+            bank += 1
+    assert all(not q for q in by_width.values())
+    assert len(result) == replicas * len(widths)
+    return result, bank
+
+
+def validate_isometries(rows, frames, roots, dimensions):
+    seen = set()
+    dot = lambda a, b: sum(x*y for x, y in zip(a, b))
+    for record in rows:
+        f = record['frame']
+        assert f not in seen
+        seen.add(f)
+        e = record['entrance_rank']
+        assert e == dimensions[f] and record['denominator'] == 2
+        basis = record['entrance_basis'] + record['residual_basis']
+        matrix = record['orthogonal_rows_numerator']
+        assert len(basis) == len(matrix) == 8
+        assert matrix == [roots[i] for i in basis]
+        assert all(len(r) == 8 and all(type(x) is int for x in r) for r in matrix)
+        assert all(dot(a,b) == 4*(i==j) for i,a in enumerate(matrix) for j,b in enumerate(matrix))
+        # The first e rows span precisely the frame, not only its dimension.
+        for i in frames[f]:
+            assert sum(dot(roots[i], q)**2 for q in matrix[:e]) == 4*dot(roots[i], roots[i])
+        assert len(record['entrance_basis']) == e
+        # This selected family needs coordinate permutations only. Checking the
+        # elementary reduction also bounds the literal route cost and primes.
+        reduced = [[x // 2 for x in row] for row in matrix]
+        assert all(x % 2 == 0 for row in matrix for x in row)
+        operations = record['gaussian_reduction']
+        assert len(operations) <= 7
+        for kind, i, j, scalar in operations:
+            assert kind == 'swap' and scalar is None and 0 <= i < 8 and 0 <= j < 8
+            reduced[i], reduced[j] = reduced[j], reduced[i]
+        assert reduced == [[int(i == j) for j in range(8)] for i in range(8)]
+    return seen

+"""Maintainer arithmetic cross-check of the pinned PR39 certificate.
+
+Uses no producer/checker imports. Counts are inputs, not proved by this script.
+80-term rational logarithms and 12-term exponentials independently enclose
+the two moments. The accompanying written review addresses their realization.
+"""
+import argparse
+from fractions import Fraction as Q
+from hashlib import sha256
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+GRID = 10**30
+
+
+def require(condition, message):
+    if not condition:
+        raise ValueError(message)
+
+
+def log_unit(x):
+    require(1 <= x <= 2, "logarithm range")
+    z = (x-1)/(x+1)
+    lo = 2*sum((z**(2*j+1)/(2*j+1) for j in range(80)), Q(0))
+    return lo, lo+2*z**161/(161*(1-z*z))
+
+
+def log_bounds(x):
+    k = 0
+    while x > 2:
+        x /= 2
+        k += 1
+    lo, hi = log_unit(x)
+    l2, u2 = log_unit(Q(2))
+    lo, hi = lo+k*l2, hi+k*u2
+    # Outward rational rounding keeps later certificates compact.
+    return Q((lo*GRID).__floor__(), GRID), Q((hi*GRID).__ceil__(), GRID)
+
+
+def exp_bounds(x):
+    require(0 <= x < 1, "exponential range")
+    term = total = Q(1)
+    for j in range(1, 13):
+        term *= x/j
+        total += term
+    tail = term*x/13/(1-x/14)
+    return total, total+tail
+
+
+def moment(m, W, entries, saving):
+    lo = hi = Q(0)
+    for t, count in entries:
+        t, count = int(t), int(count)
+        require(0 < t < m and count > 0, "improper child")
+        l, u = log_bounds(Q(m, t))
+        lower = exp_bounds(saving*l)[0]
+        upper = exp_bounds(saving*u)[1]
+        lo += Q(t*count, m*W)*lower
+        hi += Q(t*count, m*W)*upper
+    return Q((lo*GRID).__floor__(), GRID), Q((hi*GRID).__ceil__(), GRID)

+"""Exact semantic assembly with the balanced prefix, for the paired-cube network.
+
+Prepared by eumemic with Anthropic Claude assistance. Apache-2.0. The 47 strict constraints, the seven margins and
+the finite bridge are unchanged from icekylinx's scripts/structured_bulk_assembly.py (PR144, adapted from Zhihao
+Chen's PR23). The prefix is the RaD project's (hipotures) balanced positional transform, reviewed in
+references/semantic-bulk/rad20/reports/review-balanced-transform.md: the prefix margin becomes 1-eps instead of
+1-eps(1+c), and eps(1+c)<1 remains a strict geometric condition (K_geometry) whose gap need not exceed kappa.
+The parameters c=q+eta/4 and eps=(1-eta)/(1+q) are those of the reviewed balanced assembly in
+research/copied-fixed/balanced_assembly.py, with its backoff h equal to eta. Nothing else differs from
+structured_bulk_assembly.assembly.
+"""
+from fractions import Fraction as Q
+
+
+def assembly(bit_saving,complex_saving,bridge,kappa,eta=Q(1,10**8),beta=Q(1,4)):
+    a,b=bit_saving,complex_saving
+    tau,sigma=1-a,1-b
+    q=a*(1-2*eta); lp=1-q; lam=(tau+lp)/2
+    c=q+eta/4; eps=(1-eta)/(1+q)
+    minimum=eps*q; r=(minimum+1-eps)/2; delta=eta/8
+    internal=tau+(1-beta)*max(sigma-tau,Q(0));leaf=sigma+beta*(1-sigma)
+    margins=dict(balanced_prefix=1-eps,coordinate_movement=a,
+        compact_phase_layer=minimum,bulk_exposure=a,
+        Gaussian_arithmetic=min(1-eps-delta,r-delta),
+        scalar_work=1-eps-delta,dimension=eps)
+    slacks=dict(bit_positive=a,complex_above_bit=b-a,
+        complex_below_one_over32=Q(1,32)-b,beta_positive=beta,
+        beta_below_one=1-beta,leaf_saving_above_bit=(1-beta)*b-a,
+        q_positive=q,q_below_internal=1-internal-q,q_below_leaf=1-leaf-q,
+        c_positive=c,c_below_one=1-c,q_below_reservations=c-q,
+        lambda_above_tau=lam-tau,lambda_above_sigma=lam-sigma,
+        lambda_above_internal=lam-internal,lambda_prime_above_lambda=lp-lam,
+        compact_leaf=lp-leaf,compact_reservations=lp-(1-c),
+        lambda_prime_below_one=q,epsilon_positive=eps,epsilon_below_one=1-eps,
+        guard_width=1-eps,K_geometry=1-eps*(1+c),K_dominates_log=eps*c,
+        record_suffix=1-eps,phase_local=1-eps-delta,phase_boundary=r-delta,
+        gamma_sublinear=1-eps-r,cell_above_band=eps-(1-r)/2,
+        prime_interval_packing=1-eps,alpha_positive=r,alpha_below_one=1-r,
+        alpha_below_one_fourth=Q(1,4)-r,delta_positive=delta,
+        delta_below_one_eighth=Q(1,8)-delta,short_record_fallback=eps-a,
+        small_field_exposure=1-eps-minimum,
+        artificial_boundary=8-eps+r-delta-minimum,
+        literal_scalar_guard=Q(bridge['semantic']['strict_literal_gap']),
+        row_product_gap=bridge['rows']['degree_gap'])
+    slacks.update({name+'_above_kappa':val-kappa for name,val in margins.items()})
+    assert len(slacks)==47 and len(margins)==7
+    assert all(v>0 for v in slacks.values()),{k:str(v) for k,v in slacks.items() if v<=0}
+    assert min(margins.values())==minimum
+    assert margins['balanced_prefix']-minimum==eta and 1-eps-r==eta/2
+    assert 1-eps*(1+c)==eta-eps*eta/4
+    return dict(parameters=dict(a_bit=a,a_complex=b,tau=tau,sigma=sigma,
+            eta=eta,beta=beta,q=q,c=c,epsilon=eps,lambda_=lam,
+            lambda_prime=lp,alpha_squared_power=r,delta=delta,
+            C0=bridge['semantic']['C0'],C1=1,kappa=kappa),
+        strict_constraints=slacks,margins=margins,minimum_margin=minimum,
+        absorption_gap=minimum-kappa,
+        recurrence=dict(internal=internal,leaf=leaf,reservations=1-c))

+"""Export a bitE8/1 word to the PR249 record format read by PR #266's official cohort checkers and PR #315's engines.
+usage: python3 export_records.py word.json[.gz] OUTDIR   ->  OUTDIR/{249-records.bin,249-states.json,frames.json}
+Records are int32 six-tuples: MOVE(0,role,old,new,rank,0), ADD(1,dst,src,1,frame,phase), COPY(2,centre,temp,frame,ZERO,rank),
+ERASE(3,centre,temp,frame,ZERO,0).  A multi-source gate becomes one ADD per source, preceded by the MOVEs of every
+register of the gate to the gate frame.  Frames: integer basis rows B (label vectors of the frame's root lines in the
+word's coordinates, a rational basis) and integer annihilator rows A (standard dot product), as PR #266 expects.
+Dylan Crow, with Anthropic Claude assistance; Apache-2.0."""
+import sys, json, gzip, struct, os
+from fractions import Fraction as Fr
+from math import gcd
+def load(p):
+    with (gzip.open(p,'rt') if p.endswith('.gz') else open(p)) as f: return json.load(f)
+c=load(sys.argv[1]); out=sys.argv[2]; os.makedirs(out,exist_ok=True)
+v,R,h=c['v'],c['R'],c['h']; n=2*v+R; lines=c['lines']
+def basis(idx):
+    rows=[]; piv=[]; B=[]
+    for i in idx:
+        x=[Fr(a) for a in lines[i]]
+        for p,r in zip(piv,rows):
+            if x[p]: f=x[p]/r[p]; x=[a-f*b for a,b in zip(x,r)]
+        nz=[k for k in range(h) if x[k]]
+        if nz: rows.append(x); piv.append(nz[0]); B.append(list(lines[i]))
+    return B,rows,piv
+def annihilator(rows,piv):
+    # rows in echelon (pivot columns piv); free columns give the null space of the row space under the dot product
+    # reduce to RREF
+    R_=[r[:] for r in rows]
+    for i,(p,r) in enumerate(zip(piv,R_)):
+        R_[i]=[a/r[p] for a in r]
+    for i,p in enumerate(piv):
+        for j in range(len(R_)):
+            if j!=i and R_[j][p]: f=R_[j][p]; R_[j]=[a-f*b for a,b in zip(R_[j],R_[i])]
+    free=[k for k in range(h) if k not in piv]; A=[]
+    for f in free:
+        a=[Fr(0)]*h; a[f]=Fr(1)
+        for i,p in enumerate(piv): a[p]=-R_[i][f]
+        L=1
+        for x in a: L=L*x.denominator//gcd(L,x.denominator)
+        ai=[int(x*L) for x in a]; g=0
+        for x in ai: g=gcd(g,abs(x))
+        A.append([x//g for x in ai])
+    return A
+frames={}
+for k,idx in enumerate(c['frames']):
+    B,rows,piv=basis(idx); A=annihilator(rows,piv) if B else [[int(i==j) for j in range(h)] for i in range(h)]
+    assert all(sum(a*b for a,b in zip(x,y))==0 for x in A for y in B) and len(A)+len(B)==h
+    frames[str(k)]=dict(dim=len(B),B=B,A=A)
+dim=[frames[str(k)]['dim'] for k in range(len(c['frames']))]
+ZERO=[k for k in range(len(dim)) if dim[k]==0]; assert len(ZERO)==1; ZERO=ZERO[0]
+cur=list(c['start']); rec=[]
+def move(r,f):
+    if cur[r]!=f: rec.append((0,r,cur[r],f,dim[f]-dim[cur[r]],0)); cur[r]=f
+def run(gates,ph):
+    for f,d,srcs in gates:
+        for r in [d]+srcs: move(r,f)
+        for s in srcs: rec.append((1,d,s,1,f,ph))
+run(c['D'],1); run(c['A'],2)
+temp=n
+for k,q in enumerate(c['ret']):
+    fq=cur[q]; rec.append((2,q,temp,fq,ZERO,dim[fq]))
+    for t,row in enumerate(c['scatter']):
+        if k in row: rec.append((1,v+t,temp,1,ZERO,3))
+    rec.append((3,q,temp,fq,ZERO,0))
+run(c['B'],4); run(c['C'],5)
+for r in range(n): move(r,c['final'][r])
+with open(out+'/249-records.bin','wb') as f:
+    for e in rec: f.write(struct.pack('<6i',*e))
+st=dict(n=n,v=v,h=h,R=R,ZERO=ZERO,initial={str(r):c['start'][r] for r in range(n)},final={str(r):c['final'][r] for r in range(n)},
+        retained_totals=c['ret'],source_owned_roles=[],regs=[])
+json.dump(st,open(out+'/249-states.json','w'),sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':'))
+json.dump(dict(frames=frames),open(out+'/frames.json','w'),sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':'))
+print('exported',len(rec),'records,',len(frames),'frames, n',n,'ZERO',ZERO)

+# Adapted from PR #510's vendored global_k.py by research/e8-bit-p111/code/adapt9p.py. Apache-2.0.
+# Generalised from PR #443's global_kernel.py to an arbitrary odd stage count S = 2K+1 (compressed window m = 1+7S)
+# by DreamingOfClouds with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via Claude Code.  At the defaults (S = 9, 32 replicas) the emitted
+# GLOBAL-TEMPLATE.json.gz and GLOBAL.json equal PR #443's (GLOBAL.json except wall-clock seconds).
+# Kernel integration of PR436/PR386 by chafreaky, with OpenAI Codex assistance.

+"""Source-bound compressed S-stage (S = 2K+1 odd, default 9) bit template with independent replicas.
+PR386 global identity and PR436 generalization by Zhihao Chen and eumemic,
+with their disclosed OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude assistance, Apache-2.0.
+PR439 explicit residual routes and this replication extension by chafreaky,
+with OpenAI Codex assistance. All owner assignments and emitted calls are checked.
+Historical PR386 regression is performed by the unchanged parent wrapper.
+"""
+import argparse, gzip, hashlib, json, struct, time
+from collections import Counter
+from pathlib import Path
+import os, sys
+from bank_routes_k import placement, validate_isometries
+from config import REPLICAS
+
+H,L,K,T,M=8,9,4,REPLICAS,64      # overwritten in main() from --stages / --replicas
+NAMES={5:'FIVE',7:'SEVEN',9:'NINE',11:'ELEVEN',13:'THIRTEEN'}
+def sha(p): return hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+def write(p,x): p.write_text(json.dumps(x,indent=2)+'\n')
+
+def recipe(K):
+    out=[dict(kind='local',stage=0,pair=0,reverse=False)]; stage=1
+    for j in range(K):
+        out.append(dict(kind='local',stage=stage,pair=j,reverse=True)); stage+=1
+        if j<K-1: out.append(dict(kind='bridge',dst=j,src=j+1,coefficient=1))
+        out.append(dict(kind='local',stage=stage,pair=j,reverse=False)); stage+=1
+        if j<K-1: out.append(dict(kind='bridge',dst=j,src=j+1,coefficient=-1))
+    for j in reversed(range(K-1)): out.append(dict(kind='bridge',dst=j+1,src=j,coefficient=1))
+    out.append(dict(kind='exchange'))
+    return out
+
+def main():
+    ap=argparse.ArgumentParser(); ap.add_argument('--word',type=Path,required=True)
+    ap.add_argument('--local-check',type=Path,required=True); ap.add_argument('--out',type=Path,required=True)
+    ap.add_argument('--isometries',type=Path,required=True)
+    ap.add_argument('--stages',type=int,default=9); ap.add_argument('--replicas',type=int,default=REPLICAS)
+    ap.add_argument('--no-banks',action='store_true',help='emit the parent without helper bank owners (helpers are placed at hosting emission)')
+    a=ap.parse_args(); start=time.monotonic(); out=a.out; out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
+    global L,K,T,M
+    assert a.stages>=5 and a.stages%2==1; L=a.stages; K=(L-1)//2; T=a.replicas; M=1+7*L; NOBANK=a.no_banks
+    if L!=9: assert NOBANK, 'bank tiling is only emitted for the nine-stage layout; use --no-banks and host every residual'
+    DEFICIT=None   # T*(2*K*V-L*CST), set after the local replay gives CST
+    wp=a.word; w=json.loads(gzip.decompress(wp.read_bytes()) if wp.suffix=='.gz' else wp.read_bytes())
+    V,R=w['v'],w['R']; LOCAL=2*V+R; DATA=2*K*V*T; LIVE=DATA+L*R
+    assert (w['h'],w['form'])==(8,'<x,y>/2') and 100<=V<=120
+    geo=json.loads((out/'GEOMETRY.json').read_text())
+    assert geo['status']=='PASS_COMPRESSED_%s_BIT_GEOMETRY_AND_BANK_BLOCKS'%NAMES[L] and geo['stages']==L and geo['m']==M
+    # the port routes depend only on the labels: same 120 label vectors, in the same order
+    assert len(geo['ports'])==V and all(p['port']==t and p['q']==w['lines'][t] for t,p in enumerate(geo['ports']))
+    rp=a.local_check/'records/249-records.bin'; raw=rp.read_bytes(); rec=list(struct.iter_unpack('<6i',raw))
+    state=json.loads((a.local_check/'records/249-states.json').read_text())
+    fs=json.loads((a.local_check/'records/frames.json').read_text())['frames']
+    dims={int(f):z['dim'] for f,z in fs.items()}
+    lg=json.loads((a.local_check/'cout/legality.json').read_text())
+    cc=json.loads((a.local_check/'cout/columns.json').read_text())
+    assert lg['status'].startswith('PASS') and cc['status'].startswith('PASS')
+    assert (state['v'],state['n'])==(V,LOCAL) and lg['copies']==lg['erasures']==9
+    ADDS=lg['common_frame_ADDs']
+    assert cc['formal_columns_checked']==4*V+R and cc['local_scalar_additions']==ADDS
+    initial=[state['initial'][str(i)] for i in range(LOCAL)]
+    final=[state['final'][str(i)] for i in range(LOCAL)]
+    assert all(dims[final[i]]==H for i in range(2*V,LOCAL))
+    widths=[H-dims[initial[i]] for i in range(2*V,LOCAL)]
+    ENT=sum(H-z for z in widths)
+    if NOBANK: place,NB=None,None; LIVE=DATA
+    else:
+        place,NB=placement(widths,T,M)
+        assert T%8==0 and T*(H*R-ENT)%M==0 and NB==T*(H*R-ENT)//M
+        LIVE=DATA+L*NB
+    isometries=json.loads(a.isometries.read_text())
+    assert validate_isometries(isometries,w['frames'],w['lines'],dims)==set(initial[2*V:])
+    streams={}; checks={}; localH=None; CSTD=[]
+    for reverse in (False,True):
+        cur=(final if reverse else initial)[:]+[-1]; val=[1<<i for i in range(LOCAL)]+[0]
+        norm=[1]*LOCAL+[0]; maxnorm=1; center=None; hist=Counter(); events=[]; copies=0; adds=0; crs=[]
+        dim=lambda f:H-dims[f] if reverse else dims[f]
+        for op,x,y,c,f,z in (reversed(rec) if reverse else rec):
+            if op==0:
+                oldf,newf=(c,y) if reverse else (y,c)
+                assert cur[x]==oldf and dim(newf)-dim(oldf)==f>=0
+                cur[x]=newf
+                if f: hist[f]+=1
+                events.append([0,x,oldf,newf,f,int(reverse)])
+            elif op==1:
+                assert cur[x]==cur[y]==f and x!=y and x<LOCAL
+                if center is not None: assert x!=center
+                if y==LOCAL: assert center is not None
+                if c&1: val[x]^=val[y]
+                norm[x]+=abs(c)*norm[y]; maxnorm=max(maxnorm,norm[x]); adds+=1
+                events.append([1,x,y,-c if reverse else c,f,int(reverse)])
+            elif op==(3 if reverse else 2):
+                assert center is None and y==LOCAL and cur[x]==c and val[LOCAL]==0
+                copy_rank=abs(dim(c)-dim(f)); assert 0<copy_rank<=H
+                assert z==(0 if reverse else copy_rank)
+                center=x; cur[LOCAL]=f; val[LOCAL]=val[x]; norm[LOCAL]=norm[x]
+                hist[copy_rank]+=1; copies+=1; crs.append(copy_rank); events.append([2,x,LOCAL,c,f,copy_rank,int(reverse)])
+            else:
+                assert op==(2 if reverse else 3)
+                assert center==x and y==LOCAL and cur[x]==c and cur[LOCAL]==f
+                assert val[LOCAL]==val[x]
+                val[LOCAL]=0; norm[LOCAL]=0; cur[LOCAL]=-1; center=None
+                events.append([3,x,LOCAL,c,f,z,int(reverse)])
+        assert center is None and copies==9 and adds==ADDS; CSTD.append(sum(crs))
+        assert cur[:LOCAL]==(initial if reverse else final)
+        for i in range(LOCAL):
+            want=(1<<i) ^ ((1<<(i-V)) if V<=i<2*V else 0)
+            assert val[i]==want
+        assert val[LOCAL]==0
+        if localH is None: localH=hist
+        else: assert localH==hist
+        key='reverse' if reverse else 'forward'; streams[key]=events
+        checks[key]=dict(copies=copies,adds=adds,records=len(events),all_columns=LOCAL,
+                         cancellation_free_row_l1=maxnorm,profile=dict(sorted(hist.items())),
+                         sha256=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(events,separators=(',',':')).encode()).hexdigest())
+    assert CSTD[0]==CSTD[1]; CST=CSTD[0]; DEFICIT=T*(2*K*V-L*CST)   # the records' COPY ranks
+    assert sum(r*n for r,n in localH.items())==H*R-ENT+CST+2*V*(H-1)
+    assert localH==Counter({int(r):n for r,n in cc['local_raw_H']})
+
+    events=recipe(K); levels=[-1]*K; schedule=[]; bridge_controls=[]
+    # Full scalar replay on separate dirty helpers for all nine stages.
+    # Physical banking then uses the separately checked injective cover owners.
+    n=2*K*V+L*R; vals=[1<<i for i in range(n)]+[0]; temp=n
+    stages=[]
+    for e in events:
+        if e['kind']=='local':
+            s,p,rev=e['stage'],e['pair'],e['reverse']; assert levels[p]==s-1
+            def mapper(i):
+                if i==LOCAL: return temp
+                if i<2*V:
+                    side=i//V; side=1-side if rev else side
+                    return (2*p+side)*V+i%V
+                return 2*K*V+s*R+i-2*V
+            before=vals[:]; opened=False
+            for z in streams['reverse' if rev else 'forward']:
+                if z[0]==0: continue
+                x,y=mapper(z[1]),mapper(z[2])
+                if z[0]==1:
+                    if z[3]&1: vals[x]^=vals[y]
+                elif z[0]==2:
+                    assert not opened; vals[temp]=vals[x]; opened=True
+                else:
+                    assert opened and vals[temp]==vals[x]; vals[temp]=0; opened=False
+            assert not opened
+            d=(2*p+(0 if rev else 1))*V; src=(2*p+(1 if rev else 0))*V
+            for t in range(V): before[d+t]^=before[src+t]
+            assert vals==before
+            levels[p]=s; schedule.append(dict(kind='local_cover_sweep',**{k:v for k,v in e.items() if k!='kind'}))
+            if s%2==1 and s<=2*K-3:
+                j=(s+1)//2; assert levels[j]==-1; levels[j]=s
+                schedule.append(dict(kind='idle',pair=j,rank=7*(s+1),source_level=-1,target_level=s))
+            elif s%2==0 and 2<=s<=2*K-2:
+                j=s//2; assert levels[j]==s-1; levels[j]=s
+                schedule.append(dict(kind='idle',pair=j,rank=7,source_level=s-1,target_level=s))
+            elif s==2*K:
+                for j in range(K):
+                    oldlevel=levels[j]; assert oldlevel==2*j+2
+                    schedule.append(dict(kind='idle',pair=j,rank=7*(2*K-oldlevel),source_level=oldlevel,target_level=2*K))
+                    levels[j]=2*K
+            stages.append(dict(stage=s,all_columns=n,helper_columns=L*R,reverse=rev))
+        elif e['kind']=='bridge':
+            d,s=e['dst'],e['src']; assert levels[d]==levels[s]
+            for t in range(V): vals[2*d*V+t]^=vals[2*s*V+t]; vals[(2*s+1)*V+t]^=vals[(2*d+1)*V+t]
+            schedule.append(e)
+        else:
+            assert levels==[2*K]*K
+            for j in range(K):
+                for t in range(V):
+                    x=2*j*V+t; y=(2*j+1)*V+t; vals[x],vals[y]=vals[y],vals[x]
+            schedule.append(e)
+    assert vals==[1<<i for i in range(n)]+[0]
+    # Integer scalar eight-bank matrix, with each individual bridge shear omitted.
+    def small(skip=-1):
+        z=[[int(i==j) for j in range(2*K)] for i in range(2*K)]; count=0
+        def add(d,s,c): z[d]=[x+c*y for x,y in zip(z[d],z[s])]
+        for e in events:
+            if e['kind']=='local':
+                p=e['pair']; add(2*p,2*p+1,-1) if e['reverse'] else add(2*p+1,2*p,1)
+            elif e['kind']=='bridge':
+                d,s,c=e['dst'],e['src'],e['coefficient']
+                for x,y,sgn in [(2*d,2*s,c),(2*s+1,2*d+1,-c)]:
+                    if count!=skip: add(x,y,sgn)
+                    count+=1
+            else:
+                for j in range(K): z[2*j],z[2*j+1]=z[2*j+1],[-x for x in z[2*j]]
+        return z,count
+    ident=[[int(i==j) for j in range(2*K)] for i in range(2*K)]
+    z,nb=small(); assert z==ident and nb==6*(K-1)
+    for skip in range(nb): assert small(skip)[0]!=ident; bridge_controls.append(skip)
+
+    paid=Counter(); calls=[]; assignment=set(); expanded=hashlib.sha256(); full_event_count=0
+    for e in events:
+        if e['kind']!='local': continue
+        s,p,rev=e['stage'],e['pair'],e['reverse']; ori='reverse' if rev else 'forward'
+        for rep in range(T):
+            owners=[]
+            for i in range(2*V):
+                side=i//V; side=1-side if rev else side
+                owners.append([rep*(2*K*V)+(2*p+side)*V+i%V, ['data',s,i%V]])
+            for r in range(R):
+                if NOBANK: break
+                bank,offset,width=place[rep,r]
+                owners.append([DATA+s*NB+bank,['bank',offset,width,initial[2*V+r]]])
+                assignment.add((s,rep,r,bank,offset))
+            assert len({(f,tuple(route)) for f,route in owners})==(2*V if NOBANK else LOCAL)
+            assert all(0<=f<LIVE for f,route in owners)
+            # Stream one full renamed instruction program into a source-bound
+            # digest, including exact owner route descriptors and reflection.
+            for z in streams[ori]:
+                op=z[0]
+                if op==0: paid[z[4]]+=bool(z[4])
+                elif op==2: paid[z[5]]+=1
+                full_event_count+=1
+                if NOBANK: continue      # helper owners are assigned (hosted or bank) at hosting emission
+                if op==0: mapped=[op,owners[z[1]],*z[2:]]
+                else:
+                    ox=owners[z[1]]; oy=owners[z[2]] if z[2]<LOCAL else [LIVE,['private',0]]

+"""Idle-axis hosting: place whole dirty-helper residuals on the pending coordinates of an idle data family.
+
+A data family that is advanced by an idle child from level a to level b receives the commuting coordinate factors of
+that child.  If the family is untouched (no local invocation on its pair and no bridge naming its pair) during an
+interval of local invocations ending at the child, a helper residual of width w from an invocation inside that
+interval may own w of those pending coordinates instead of a bank slot.  The child keeps only the remaining
+coordinates.  This module computes the windows from the recipe and chooses, per replica, how many residuals of each
+width each child hosts (exact integer programme), then expands that choice into explicit slot assignments.
+Standard library plus scipy for the integer programme; the emitted assignment is re-checked without scipy."""
+import math
+from collections import Counter, defaultdict
+
+def windows(schedule):
+    """schedule: ordered events dict(kind='local',stage,pair) | dict(kind='bridge',dst,src) | dict(kind='idle',pair,rank,idx).
+    Returns {idx: (pair, rank, frozenset(stages))} - stages whose invocation lies strictly between the last touch of
+    the pair and the idle child."""
+    last = {}; out = {}; locals_ = []
+    for pos, e in enumerate(schedule):
+        k = e['kind']
+        if k == 'local':
+            locals_.append((pos, e['stage'], e['pair'])); last[e['pair']] = pos
+        elif k == 'bridge':
+            last[e['dst']] = pos; last[e['src']] = pos
+        elif k == 'idle':
+            p = e['pair']; lo = last.get(p, -1)
+            st = frozenset(s for q, s, pp in locals_ if lo < q < pos and pp != p)
+            out[e['idx']] = (p, e['rank'], st)      # an idle child acts on other coordinates (or the other member): not a touch
+    return out
+
+def patterns(rank, widths, maxk=12):
+    """multisets of widths with sum <= rank (as sorted tuples)"""
+    ws = sorted(set(widths), reverse=True); res = []
+    def rec(i, cur, s):
+        if i == len(ws): res.append(tuple(cur)); return
+        w = ws[i]; k = 0
+        while s + k * w <= rank and len(cur) + k <= maxk:
+            rec(i + 1, cur + [w] * k, s + k * w); k += 1
+    rec(0, [], 0)
+    return res
+
+def cost(r, m):
+    return r * math.log(m / r) if r else 0.0
+
+def solve(win, copies, avail, m, pad_value=0.0, group=None):
+    """win: {idx: (pair, rank, stages)}; copies: piece copies per replica of each idx (2V);
+    avail: {(stage, width): count per replica}; maximise saved idle cost (+ pad_value per hosted residual).
+    group: optional {width: g} - remaining count of that width per stage must be a multiple of g (exact bank tiling).
+    Returns {(idx, pattern): copies} and {(idx, width, stage): count}."""
+    import numpy as np
+    from scipy.optimize import milp, LinearConstraint, Bounds
+    widths = sorted({w for (_, w) in avail})
+    var = []; index = {}
+    for idx, (p, r, st) in win.items():
+        for pat in patterns(r, widths):
+            index[('y', idx, pat)] = len(var); var.append(('y', idx, pat))
+        for w in widths:
+            for s in st:
+                if avail.get((s, w), 0):
+                    index[('z', idx, w, s)] = len(var); var.append(('z', idx, w, s))
+    stages = sorted({s for (s, _) in avail})
+    if group:
+        for w, g in group.items():
+            for s in stages:
+                index[('g', w, s)] = len(var); var.append(('g', w, s))
+    n = len(var); c = np.zeros(n); integ = np.ones(n); lb = np.zeros(n); ub = np.full(n, np.inf)
+    for key, j in index.items():
+        if key[0] == 'y':
+            _, idx, pat = key; r = win[idx][1]; c[j] = -(cost(r, m) - cost(r - sum(pat), m) + pad_value * len(pat))
+    rows, lo, hi = [], [], []
+    for idx in win:
+        row = np.zeros(n)
+        for key, j in index.items():
+            if key[0] == 'y' and key[1] == idx: row[j] = 1
+        rows.append(row); lo.append(copies); hi.append(copies)
+        for w in widths:
+            row = np.zeros(n)
+            for key, j in index.items():
+                if key[0] == 'y' and key[1] == idx: row[j] = key[2].count(w)
+                if key[0] == 'z' and key[1] == idx and key[2] == w: row[j] = -1
+            rows.append(row); lo.append(0); hi.append(0)
+    for (s, w), a in avail.items():
+        row = np.zeros(n)
+        for key, j in index.items():
+            if key[0] == 'z' and key[2] == w and key[3] == s: row[j] = 1
+        if group and w in group:
+            row[index[('g', w, s)]] = group[w]; rows.append(row); lo.append(a); hi.append(a)   # used + g*k = avail
+        else:
+            rows.append(row); lo.append(0); hi.append(a)
+    res = milp(c, constraints=LinearConstraint(np.array(rows), lo, hi), integrality=integ, bounds=Bounds(lb, ub),
+               options=dict(time_limit=600, disp=False))
+    assert res.x is not None, res.message
+    x = [int(round(t)) for t in res.x]
+    ys = {(k[1], k[2]): x[j] for k, j in index.items() if k[0] == 'y' and x[j]}
+    zs = {(k[1], k[2], k[3]): x[j] for k, j in index.items() if k[0] == 'z' and x[j]}
+    return ys, zs, -res.fun
+
+def expand(win, ys, zs, helpers, V2):
+    """helpers: {stage: [(helper, width), ...]} for ONE replica; returns list of
+    (idx, copy, offset, width, stage, helper) and the remainder rank of every (idx, copy).
+    Copies of a piece are the 2V (side, port) data families; residuals packed from offset 0 in decreasing width."""
+    pool = defaultdict(list)                    # (stage, width) -> helpers
+    for s, hs in helpers.items():
+        for h, w in hs: pool[s, w].append(h)
+    for k in pool: pool[k].sort()
+    need = defaultdict(list)                    # (idx, width) -> stages multiset in deterministic order
+    for (idx, w, s), cnt in sorted(zs.items()): need[idx, w] += [s] * cnt
+    out = []; rem = {}
+    for idx in sorted(win):
+        pats = sorted([(pat, cnt) for (i, pat), cnt in ys.items() if i == idx], key=lambda t: (-sum(t[0]), t[0]))
+        copy = 0; ptr = Counter()
+        r = win[idx][1]
+        for pat, cnt in pats:
+            for _ in range(cnt):
+                off = 0
+                for w in sorted(pat, reverse=True):
+                    s = need[idx, w][ptr[idx, w]]; ptr[idx, w] += 1
+                    h = pool[s, w].pop(0)
+                    out.append((idx, copy, off, w, s, h)); off += w
+                rem[idx, copy] = r - off; copy += 1
+        while copy < V2: rem[idx, copy] = r; copy += 1
+    return out, rem
+
+def save_selection(path, key, ys, zs, val):
+    """freeze the integer-programme choice (patterns per child, residual stages per child) for stdlib-only replay"""
+    import json
+    from pathlib import Path
+    p = Path(path); d = json.loads(p.read_text()) if p.exists() else {}
+    d[key] = dict(patterns=sorted([[i, list(pat), n] for (i, pat), n in ys.items()]),
+                  stages=sorted([[i, w, s, n] for (i, w, s), n in zs.items()]), proxy_saving=val)
+    p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + '\n')
+
+def load_selection(path, key):
+    import json
+    from pathlib import Path
+    d = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())[key]
+    ys = {(i, tuple(pat)): n for i, pat, n in d['patterns']}
+    zs = {(i, w, s): n for i, w, s, n in d['stages']}
+    return ys, zs, d['proxy_saving']

+imported unchanged from DaysSky's PR #442 (research/idle-axis-hosting/hosting_core.py).
+
+solve() is PR #442's HC.solve with
+  * host_all:      every helper residual of every stage must be hosted (no bank is left; used when the compressed
+                   window m is not tileable by the residual widths, e.g. m = 78);
+  * max_remainder: every idle child must keep at most this many coordinates (halving-depth control).
+With both options off it is the same programme as HC.solve (same variables, rows and objective), so --discover at
+the nine-stage defaults reproduces the frozen PR #442/#444 selections.
+Generalised by DreamingOfClouds with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via Claude Code.  Apache-2.0.
+"""
+import os, sys
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+import hosting_core as HC
+windows, patterns, cost, expand, save_selection, load_selection = HC.windows, HC.patterns, HC.cost, HC.expand, HC.save_selection, HC.load_selection
+
+def solve(win, copies, avail, m, pad_value=0.0, group=None, host_all=False, max_remainder=None, maxk=12, time_limit=600):
+    import numpy as np
+    from scipy.optimize import milp, LinearConstraint, Bounds
+    widths = sorted({w for (_, w) in avail})
+    var = []; index = {}
+    for idx, (p, r, st) in win.items():
+        for pat in patterns(r, widths, maxk):
+            if max_remainder is not None and r - sum(pat) > max_remainder: continue
+            index[('y', idx, pat)] = len(var); var.append(('y', idx, pat))
+        for w in widths:
+            for s in st:
+                if avail.get((s, w), 0):
+                    index[('z', idx, w, s)] = len(var); var.append(('z', idx, w, s))
+    stages = sorted({s for (s, _) in avail})
+    if group:
+        for w, g in group.items():
+            for s in stages:
+                index[('g', w, s)] = len(var); var.append(('g', w, s))
+    n = len(var); c = np.zeros(n); integ = np.ones(n); lb = np.zeros(n); ub = np.full(n, np.inf)
+    for key, j in index.items():
+        if key[0] == 'y':
+            _, idx, pat = key; r = win[idx][1]; c[j] = -(cost(r, m) - cost(r - sum(pat), m) + pad_value * len(pat))
+    rows, lo, hi = [], [], []
+    for idx in win:
+        row = np.zeros(n)
+        for key, j in index.items():
+            if key[0] == 'y' and key[1] == idx: row[j] = 1
+        rows.append(row); lo.append(copies); hi.append(copies)
+        for w in widths:
+            row = np.zeros(n)
+            for key, j in index.items():
+                if key[0] == 'y' and key[1] == idx: row[j] = key[2].count(w)
+                if key[0] == 'z' and key[1] == idx and key[2] == w: row[j] = -1
+            rows.append(row); lo.append(0); hi.append(0)
+    for (s, w), a in avail.items():
+        row = np.zeros(n)
+        for key, j in index.items():
+            if key[0] == 'z' and key[2] == w and key[3] == s: row[j] = 1
+        if group and w in group:
+            row[index[('g', w, s)]] = group[w]; rows.append(row); lo.append(a); hi.append(a)   # used + g*k = avail
+        elif host_all:
+            rows.append(row); lo.append(a); hi.append(a)
+        else:
+            rows.append(row); lo.append(0); hi.append(a)
+    res = milp(c, constraints=LinearConstraint(np.array(rows), lo, hi), integrality=integ, bounds=Bounds(lb, ub),

+    x = [int(round(t)) for t in res.x]
+    ys = {(k[1], k[2]): x[j] for k, j in index.items() if k[0] == 'y' and x[j]}
+    zs = {(k[1], k[2], k[3]): x[j] for k, j in index.items() if k[0] == 'z' and x[j]}
+    return ys, zs, -res.fun

+"""Residual census (8 - sigma per helper) and an exact zero-padding bank tiling of width m = (2K+1)h with T replicas:
+tile() and economy_tile() verbatim from our PR #329 bank_template.py (via code/tile.py of our dtst3 package).

+import sys,os,collections
+from collections import Counter
+sys.path.insert(0,os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+from e8core import *
+def economy_tile(blocks, m):
+    """Exact zero-padding tiling used when the filler search of tile() runs out of filler blocks (the kernel pivots
+    and early restorations of the stage stack add many residual widths that do not divide m; the PR #299 analogue at
+    p = 12 was the (r^4, 24, 4^(24-r)) re-tiling). The fillers are the two most numerous widths dividing m (here the
+    full helper width h and the rank-4 entrance residual). Each other width w, in decreasing order, gets the bank
+    w^a F^c f^b (w*a + F*c + f*b = m) that spends the fewest narrow fillers f per w block (then the largest a), plus
+    at most one bank w^r F^c' f^b' for the remainder r = n mod a. The leftover fillers fill pure banks F^(m/F),
+    f^(m/f) and y residue banks F^j f^k. Every bank sums to m and every block is used exactly once (no padding)."""
+    from fractions import Fraction
+    blocks = {w: n for w, n in blocks.items() if n}
+    div = sorted((w for w in blocks if m % w == 0), key=lambda w: (-blocks[w], w))
+    assert len(div) >= 2, ('economy tiling needs two filler widths', blocks)
+    F, f = sorted(div[:2], reverse=True)
+
+    def fill(rest):
+        """(c, b) with F*c + f*b = rest, c maximal (fewest narrow fillers); None if impossible."""
+        return next(((c, (rest - F*c)//f) for c in range(rest//F, -1, -1) if (rest - F*c) % f == 0), None)

+    left = {F: blocks[F], f: blocks[f]}; out = []

+        n = blocks[w]

+        assert opts, ('no bank for width', w)

+        if q: out.append(((w,)*a + (F,)*c + (f,)*b, q)); left[F] -= q*c; left[f] -= q*b
+        if r:

+                out += ([((F,)*j + (f,)*k, y)] if y else []) + ([((F,)*pF, aF//pF)] if aF else []) + ([((f,)*pf, af//pf)] if af else [])
+                return out

+
+
+def tile(blocks, m):
+    """Exact tiling of {width: number of blocks} into banks of total width m, as ((widths, banks), ...).
+
+    A width dividing m fills pure banks. A width w not dividing m is mixed with a filler width f dividing m:
+    banks w^a f^b with a maximal (w*a + f*b = m), then at most one bank w^r f^t for the remainder r. Fillers
+    are tried in a fixed order (most blocks first) with backtracking until every pure width also divides out.
+    Fails (AssertionError) unless every block is used and every bank is full; there is no padding."""
+    blocks = {w: n for w, n in blocks.items() if n}
+    assert all(0 < w <= m for w in blocks)
+    mixed = sorted(x for x in blocks if m % x)
+
+    def search(i, left, out):
+        if i == len(mixed):
+            if any(left[w] % (m // w) for w in left): return None
+            return out + [(tuple([w]*(m // w)), left[w]//(m // w)) for w in sorted(left) if left[w]]
+        w = mixed[i]; n = blocks[w]
+        for f in sorted(left, key=lambda x: (-left[x], x)):

+            if a is None: continue
+            b = (m - w*a)//f; q, r = divmod(n, a)
+            if r and (m - w*r) % f: continue

+            found = search(i + 1, rest, out + ([(tuple([w]*a + [f]*b), q)] if q else []) + ([(tuple([w]*r + [f]*t), 1)] if r else []))
+            if found is not None: return found

+    out = search(0, {w: n for w, n in blocks.items() if not m % w}, [])

+    for widths, count in out:

+"""Independent exact replay and interface audit of a bitE8/1 word with v <= 120 live ports (a punctured word: some
+E8 root lines are neither sources nor targets) whose source and helper registers may be gate destinations in phase A
+and in phase B (interleaved with target reads).  No producer, generator or hub code is imported; only the word file is
+read.  Adapted from the R420 package's code/xcheck.py (v = 120) by exact edits: the label count, frame closure and
+target frames are taken over the v live labels, and Part T is added.
+usage: xcheck_p.py WORD.json.gz [--json OUT]
+
+Part L (labels): the v labels are integer vectors with <x,y> = dot/2; every label has norm 2, distinct labels have
+|<a,b>| <= 1, and the lattice they generate (Hermite normal form over Z) has Gram determinant 1 and rank 8.  An even
+unimodular positive definite lattice of rank 8 is E8, so the labels are root lines of it.  The root lines of that
+lattice are enumerated (all vectors of norm 2 among the integer vectors with entries in {-2..2} that lie in the
+lattice: 240 roots, 120 lines); the punctured lines are the root lines that are not labels.  Every listed frame is
+closed in the live labels (the listed lines are exactly the labels in its span).

+class Reject(Exception):

+# ------------------------------------------------------------------ exact linear algebra over Q and Z
+def rref(rows):
+    """reduced row echelon form over Q of integer rows; returns (basis rows, pivot columns)"""
+    m = [[Fraction(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
+    piv = []
+    rk = 0
+    ncol = len(m[0]) if m else 0
+    for col in range(ncol):
+        p = next((i for i in range(rk, len(m)) if m[i][col] != 0), None)
+        if p is None:
+            continue
+        m[rk], m[p] = m[p], m[rk]
+        inv = 1 / m[rk][col]
+        m[rk] = [a * inv for a in m[rk]]
+        for i in range(len(m)):
+            if i != rk and m[i][col] != 0:
+                f = m[i][col]
+                m[i] = [a - f * b for a, b in zip(m[i], m[rk])]
+        piv.append(col)
+        rk += 1
+    return m[:rk], piv

+def nullspace_int(rows, ncol=8):
+    """integer basis of {n : r.n = 0 for every row r} (dot product)"""
+    if not rows:
+        return [[int(i == j) for j in range(ncol)] for i in range(ncol)]
+    basis, piv = rref(rows)
+    free = [c for c in range(ncol) if c not in piv]
+    out = []
+    for f in free:
+        vec = [Fraction(0)] * ncol
+        vec[f] = Fraction(1)
+        for r, pc in zip(basis, piv):
+            vec[pc] = -r[f]
+        den = 1
+        for x in vec:
+            den = den * x.denominator // math.gcd(den, x.denominator)
+        out.append([int(x * den) for x in vec])
+    return out

+def hnf_basis(rows):
+    """Z-basis of the lattice generated by integer rows (row-style Hermite reduction)"""
+    m = [list(r) for r in rows if any(r)]
+    basis = []
+    ncol = len(rows[0])
+    for col in range(ncol):
+        m = [r for r in m if any(r)]
+        while True:
+            nz = [r for r in m if r[col] != 0]
+            if len(nz) <= 1:
+                break

+            p = nz[0]
+            for r in m:
+                if r is not p and r[col] != 0:
+                    q = r[col] // p[col]
+                    for j in range(ncol):

+        nz = [r for r in m if r[col] != 0]
+        if nz:
+            basis.append(nz[0])
+            m = [r for r in m if r is not nz[0]]
+    return basis

+def det(M):
+    M = [[Fraction(x) for x in r] for r in M]

+        p = next((i for i in range(col, n) if M[i][col] != 0), None)
+        if p is None:
+            return Fraction(0)
+        if p != col:
+            M[col], M[p] = M[p], M[col]
+            d = -d
+        d *= M[col][col]
+        for i in range(col + 1, n):
+            f = M[i][col] / M[col][col]
+            M[i] = [a - f * b for a, b in zip(M[i], M[col])]
+    return d

+# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the checker
